domain_restrictions: q is a formal indeterminate, not a numeric parameter
The product index i is an integer
If a = b, the product is empty and equals 1
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: If integers a, b, r satisfy 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, and if for every positive integer d the floor inequality floor((r + b) / d) - floor((r + a) / d) >= floor(b / d) - floor(a / d) holds, then the finite product from i = a + 1 to b of (1 - q to the power r + i) divided by (1 - q to the power i) is a polynomial with integer coefficients, and every coefficient is at least 0.
quantifier_order: For all integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0
Define P of a, b, r at q by the finite product over i from a + 1 to b, with empty product equal to 1 when a = b
For all positive integers d, the floor inequality holds: floor((r + b) / d) - floor((r + a) / d) >= floor(b / d) - floor(a / d)
Then P of a, b, r at q is a polynomial in the integer polynomial ring and all of its coefficients are nonnegative

variables.domain: formal variable for the polynomial ring over the integers
variables.name: q

witness_dependencies: No existential witnesses are asserted; the statement is a universal implication from the floor condition to polynomiality and coefficient nonnegativity

statement_nl: Let a, b, r be integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0. Define P_{a,b,r}(q) := product_{i=a+1}^{b} ((1 - q^(r+i)) / (1 - q^i)), with empty product equal to 1. Assume that for every positive integer d one has floor((r+b)/d) - floor((r+a)/d) >= floor(b/d) - floor(a/d). Then P_{a,b,r}(q) is a polynomial in Z[q], and every coefficient of P_{a,b,r}(q) is nonnegative.
